name: Dipropanoylmorphine
summary: Dipropanoylmorphine (dipropionylmorphine in US English) is an opiate derivative, the 3,6-dipropanoyl ester of morphine. It was developed in 1972 as an analgesic. It is rarely used in some countries for the relief of severe pain such as that caused by terminal cancer, as an alternative to diamorphine (heroin) and morphine.

uses.text: It is rarely used in some countries for the relief of severe pain such as that caused by terminal cancer, as an alternative to diamorphine (heroin) and morphine. Dipropanoylmorphine, though rarely used, is considered to be a safer and less addictive alternative to morphine. Propanoic anhydride however is much less widely used.

sideEffects.text: Side effects are generally relatively mild for an opioid with a similar profile to morphine/heroin and typical of other opioids. The most common side effects associated with dipropanoylmorphine are itching, nausea and respiratory depression.
